title: Adaptive backpressure and prioritized admission control for multi-region failover
creator: Amelia Zhang
description: Problem: During cross-region outages we observe sudden traffic surges that exceed local capacity. Current shedding is binary and global: whole model variants are dropped or global rate limits trigger, which causes severe user-visible failures for high-priority tenants and long tail requests. We need a region-aware, priority-sensitive backpressure system that applies graceful degradation at multiple levels (request admission, per-tenant soft caps, response-quality degradation) and coordinates with circuit breakers to avoid cascading failures.
acceptance_criteria: A region-aware admission controller is implemented that enforces prioritized lanes (system, SLA, best-effort) and can demote or delay best-effort traffic under contention
Per-tenant soft caps are configurable via Console and enforced by admission control with metrics exposed (rejection_rate, queued_ms, demotion_count)
A graceful degradation policy exists that can switch routes from full-generation -> reduced-token -> metadata-only modes dynamically and independently per tenant/route
Circuit-breaker integration: when downstream model latency/error thresholds are crossed, controller triggers demotion of low-priority lanes and opens a short circuit for non-essential paths
Canary rollout in two regions with traffic shaping and automated rollback if SLO regressions exceed thresholds
Dashboard shows per-region lane utilization, dropped_requests_by_reason, and per-tenant SLOs; alerts fire on >1% high-priority rejection over 5m or >10% latency p99 regression
design_decisions: Use lane-based admission rather than single global token queue to allow targeted shedding and visibility
Admission controller runs as a sidecar in edge proxies and as a centralized control-plane policy for cross-region decisions
Demotion strategy: prefer reducing compute (reduced-token) before outright rejecting for tenants with medium SLAs; best-effort tenants can be rejected earlier
Circuit-breaker thresholds are conservative to avoid flip-flopping: 3s p95 latency or 10% error rate sustained over 30s triggers demotion
Backpressure signal uses token-based budget accounting (remaining_compute_budget) per route/tenant to prevent head-of-line blocking
Configuration exposed via Console + API with default safe profiles to avoid accidental total denial of service for new tenants
rollout_plan: 1) Merge admission-controller feature flag behind runtime-2.4.0 feature toggle
2) Deploy sidecar to staging region and run synthetic workload to validate lane enforcement and metrics
3) Canary deploy to us-west-2 with 5% of traffic for 48 hours; observe SLOs and demotion rates
4) Gradually ramp target regions to 25% then 100% while validating rollback triggers
5) Enable Console controls for tenant soft caps; coordinate with solutions engineering for top 20 customers
6) Post-rollout 2-week monitoring window and incident retro
monitoring_and_alerts: Metrics: lane_utilization_{region, lane}, admission_queue_length, queued_ms_p95, demotion_count_by_tenant, rejection_rate_by_lane
SLO monitoring: per-tenant request_success_rate and p99_latency compared to baseline; automatic regression detection via existing eval pipeline
Alerts: P1 if high-priority rejection_rate > 0.01 for 5m; P2 for demotion_count spike > 500/min across a region
Dashboards: multi-region backpressure overview, per-tenant SLO panel, circuit-breaker state timeline
Runbook: immediate steps to scale Dedicated pools, enable cross-region failover, and toggle demotion severity in Console
updates: 2025-10-15 - Amelia Zhang: Initial spike analysis attached; identified correlation between region failover events and increased KV cache misses leading to higher per-token latency.
2025-10-22 - Ravi Patel: Prototype lane-based admission controller implemented; local testing shows 30% reduction in high-priority rejections under synthetic overload.
2025-10-30 - Design review (Sofia Martinez): UI flows for tenant soft caps and demotion policies approved with minor wording changes for Console labels.
2025-11-02 - Security review kickoff: SRE and Security validated that admission control sidecar does not retain PII; no additional keys needed.
2025-11-05 - Ravi Patel: Canary plan finalized; canary thresholds updated after SLO simulation to use 5% p99 uplift as rollback trigger. Preparing k8s manifests for sidecar deployment.
comments: PM (Diego Ramos) - 2025-10-23: Prioritize ensuring high-tier customers never see full rejects. Make default profiles conservative.
SRE (Lin Wei) - 2025-10-28: We should ensure admission controller metrics are high-cardinality safe; avoid per-request labels that explode cardinality.
Engineering (Priya Singh) - 2025-11-01: Suggest adding an emergency bypass for billing/console operations to avoid operational deadlock during a failover.
Design (Sofia Martinez) - 2025-10-30: Recommend adding a timeline visualization for demotion events in Console to aid post-incident analysis.
